# dsh-notify
English · 简体中文
> A DSH plugin that raises a native desktop notification when a Session finishes while DeepSeek Harn
ess is not the focused app — click the banner to jump straight back to that Session.
Sessions in DSH run for minutes at a time. When you switch to another app you should not have to kee
p checking the window: **dsh-notify** watches the Session list and, on every `running: true → false`
edge, decides whether you are already looking at that conversation. If you are not, it posts a noti
fication through the browser `Notification` API, which the DSH desktop shell turns into a real macOS
Notification Center / Windows Action Center / Linux desktop notification, with the DeepSeek Harness
app icon and the system sound.
It occupies no UI slots, has no settings, sends nothing over the network, and needs no host service.
## Features
### When a notification is raised
| Situation | Notifies? |
| A task finishes while DSH is in the background (another app focused / minimised / page hidden) | ✅

Yes — native system notification |
| A task finishes while you are literally looking at that conver

sation (window in front **and** `retainedBy.mainView > 0`) | ❌ No — you can already see it |
| DSH i
s in front, but **another** Session finishes | ✅ Yes — chat-app semantics: other conversations still

announce |
| A subagent / Agent Teams teammate finishes | ❌ No — the Lead Session reports completio

n instead |
| A task was already running when the page loaded | ✅ Yes, but without duration text |
|
A task started after the page loaded | ✅ Yes, with duration text such as `Task completed in 3m 5s ·
fter the page loaded | ✅ Yes, with duration text such as `Task completed in 3m 5s · Click to open` |
"Which conversation am I looking at" is not guessed. The main view retains the Session it is showing
, and the Session list row carries that knowledge as `retainedBy.mainView > 0` — the same field the
shipped shell uses for every "current Session" read. The window must also be in front: `document.vis
ibilityState === 'visible'` **and** `document.hasFocus()`.
### Everything else
- **Click to open.** Dismiss the banner, focus the DSH window, and open the Session it names (via th

e client `uiWorkspace` service).
- **No banner pile-up.** Each Session uses a stable notification `t
ag` (`dsh-notify:<session-id>`), so a repeat completion replaces the previous banner instead of stac

king a second one.
[该节后续省略]
### Requirements
| Requirement | Value |

| DSH | Tested with `0.2.2-rc.1`; needs the Web UI and its Client plugin API |
| Node.js | `>= 20` |

| Runtime dependencies | None |
| OS notifications | Native notifications are delivered by the Elec
tron shell; allow them for DeepSeek Harness in the OS settings |
The default profile is usually `web` (the one `dsh web` uses). Run `dsh plugin --profile web list` i
le is usually `web` (the one `dsh web` uses). Run `dsh plugin --profile web list` if you are unsure.
## How it works
- **Host half** (`index.js`) is intentionally inert. It exists so the bundle patch can mount the plu

gin row and publish its Client module; all behaviour lives in the browser.
- **Client half** (`clien

t.js`) registers one Cordis plugin and injects the `sessions` and `locale` services.
- It subscribes
to `ctx.sessions.list`, the Client's Host-authoritative Session list. Rows carry `running`, so the
watcher can keep a map of the Sessions it has observed running and react to each `true → false` edge

.
- **Priming:** the live list starts as `phase: 'pending'` with no rows. The watcher waits for the
first `ready` snapshot; a Session that is already running then is recorded with an *unknown* start,

so it never reports a bogus duration measured from page load.
- **The suppression decision** happens

once per completion edge:
- `parentId !== undefined` or `origin === 'subagent'` → subagent / teamma

te, stay silent;
- `pageInFront() && retainedBy.mainView > 0` → you are looking at it, stay silent;

- everything else → notify.
- **Delivery:** `new Notification(title, { body, tag })` inside the `dsh
-app://app` page. Electron routes browser notifications to the OS, so the banner appears in Notifica

tion Center / Action Center / the desktop notification daemon.
- **Click handling:** `notification.o
nclick` closes the banner, calls `window.focus()` (best effort), and asks the `uiWorkspace` service

to open the Session.
- **Localization:** both dictionaries are registered under the `dsh-notify` nam

espace; if the locale service is not ready yet, the bundled tables are used directly.
- **Tracing:**
every interesting step writes one JSON object to `localStorage['dsh-notify:trace']` — `loaded`, an
`edge` record with `subagent` / `foreground` / `watching` flags, or `notified`.
## Data & privacy
- **No network access.** The plugin never calls `fetch`, WebSocket, or any host route; there is no t

elemetry.
- **No host state.** The Host half declares no service and writes nothing.
- **One local w
rite.** `localStorage['dsh-notify:trace']` holds a single overwritten diagnostic object (see below).

It can be deleted at any time and only exists in that browser profile.
- **Notification content sta
ys on the machine.** The title is the Session title (or the workspace folder name), and the body is

fixed localized copy plus the observed duration.
- **Nothing is published anywhere.** Uninstalling t
he plugin leaves only that localStorage key behind; clearing it is harmless.
The diagnostic breadcrumb is the quickest way to confirm the plugin is running and why a given compl
etion did or did not produce a banner:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Compatibility
- **Platforms:** macOS, Windows and Linux through the DSH desktop app. In a plain browser (`dsh web`

opened in a tab) browser notification permission and tab liveness apply instead.
- **Liveness:** th
e page must be alive. Closing the window so the app exits means no process can raise a notification.
- **DSH plugin API:** the client side reads `ctx.sessions.list` snapshots and the `retainedBy.mainV
iew` field of each row. Those are stable DSH Web UI structures today, but they are internal APIs: a

future DSH release could rename them and require a plugin update.
- **No dependencies:** the plugin
is plain ES modules and browser APIs only; nothing to build.
